## Page 1 | H7-A: Pilot evidence and model assumptions

GreenWaste is a fictional training case. Use this summary to check every claim made in the session.

### §1 | The pilot RCT result

A lottery assigned **200 eligible businesses** in one pilot district to GreenWaste and **200** to a control group. Annual waste management cost was measured at 12 months. The treatment-minus-control estimate is **`r fmt(case$rct)` AED** per business (95% interval **`r fmt(case$rct_ci[1])` to `r fmt(case$rct_ci[2])` AED**). On a saving scale, the estimate is **`r fmt(model$saving)` AED per business per year**, with a 95% interval from **`r fmt(min(-case$rct_ci))` to `r fmt(max(-case$rct_ci))` AED**. Assignment supports a causal interpretation in the pilot if implementation and measurement remain credible. It does not establish effects in other districts or over five years.

### §2 | Which economic question?

| Method | Outcome unit | A question it can answer |
|---|---|---|
| Cost-effectiveness analysis (CEA) | Natural unit | AED per tonne of landfill avoided |
| Cost-utility analysis (CUA) | Health utility, often QALYs | AED per QALY gained |
| Cost-benefit analysis (CBA) | Money | Net benefit in AED or benefit-cost ratio |

CUA is a form of CEA. The pilot's measured waste-cost outcome is in AED and can be considered as a monetary benefit, subject to a clear perspective and what the bill reduction represents. This handout works through a **partial monetary model**, not a complete social CBA. It has no causal landfill-effect or QALY calculation for CEA or CUA.

### §3 | Inputs to the worked model

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d7_inputs('Table I: Per pilot business'))
```

The model treats the RCT's 12-month annual-cost difference as a **year-1 saving**, then assumes that the same saving persists in **years 2 to 5**. It assumes **1,800 AED** in delivery cost at year 0 and a **5%** annual discount rate. Only the 12-month difference is estimated from the RCT. The cost, persistence and discount rate are teaching assumptions, not audited or official inputs. Calculations use unrounded values; displayed amounts are rounded.

### §4 | Whose costs and benefits?

The assumed cost is paid by the **authority**. The measured financial saving is for **businesses**. Staff time, business maintenance and wider environmental effects have not been valued. A lower bill may reflect saved resources or a transfer between actors. This ratio is neither an authority budget return nor a complete social benefit-cost analysis. Specify the perspective and check what is already counted before adding entries.

<p class="source-note">Method references: CDC, Cost-Effectiveness Analysis; NICE, Health Technology Evaluations Manual; HM Treasury, The Green Book (2026). The fictional model does not claim to follow an official discount rate.</p>

</div>

## Page 2 | H7-A: Timing, results and sensitivity

### §5 | Cash flow per pilot business

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d7_cash_table('Table F: AED per business; each saving shown at its year-0 present value'))
```

For year 1, the value today of the annual saving is **`r fmt(model$saving)` / 1.05 = `r fmt(model$saving/1.05)` AED**. The savings in years 2 to 5 are divided by 1.05 raised to their respective year numbers. Their persistence is assumed, not observed in the RCT.

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d7_output('Table O: Worked model, per pilot business'))
```

The benefit-cost ratio is present-value benefits divided by present-value costs; it has **no units**. Net present benefit is the difference, in **AED**. Under this model, an annual saving of about **`r fmt(model$cost/pv_factor())` AED** gives a ratio of 1. That model break-even level differs from the separate policy rule of at least **1,000 AED annual waste-cost saving**. The RCT interval crosses the policy rule. It is not a confidence interval for the benefit-cost ratio.

### §6 | Change the assumption, then check the result

| Scenario | Modelled ratio |
|---|---:|
| Base model | `r fmt(ratio(),2)` |
| Savings fade by 30% after the first saving year | `r fmt(ratio(decay=.3),2)` |
| Add 600 AED to year-0 delivery cost | `r fmt(ratio(extra=600),2)` |
| Discount at 8% instead of 5% | `r fmt(ratio(rate=.08),2)` |
| Savings last three years rather than five | `r fmt(ratio(years=3),2)` |
| Savings fade by 30% and add 800 AED cost | `r fmt(ratio(decay=.3,extra=800),2)` |

These are hypothetical settings, not findings about GreenWaste. The final scenario changes two inputs. Their ranking depends on the values chosen. Programme accounts, follow-up data and applicable appraisal guidance would help determine realistic inputs.

## Page 4 | Question the result and advise

### Q5 | Two thresholds (H7-A §5)

The model breaks even at about **`r fmt(model$cost/pv_factor())` AED** annual saving. The policy minimum is **1,000 AED** annual saving.

(a) Does the pilot RCT interval of 862 to 1,167 AED sit entirely above either threshold? Explain the difference.
<div class="writing tall"></div>

(b) Name an assumption that could move the model break-even level.
